key_insight: MANTRA tests whether early angiotensin-II, versus norepinephrine, can better correct septic-shock RAAS dysfunction and reshape immune responses.
clinical_relevance: If effective, this approach could support a more mechanism-guided vasopressor strategy in septic shock rather than relying only on norepinephrine escalation.
method: Multicenter, open-label, randomized mechanistic trial in adults with septic shock.
1:1 assignment to primary angiotensin-II or norepinephrine for 48 hours.
Primary endpoint: change in plasma renin from baseline to 24 hours; secondary endpoints include vasopressor needs, organ-support outcomes, and biomarker/immune measures.
evidence_signal: The abstract describes a prospective randomized trial with n=78 powered to detect a 25% between-group difference in 24-hour renin, using longitudinal mixed-effects analysis.
watch_item: Because this is a protocol and open-label design, results may be influenced by implementation differences and may not yet establish clinical benefit.
paper_title: Mechanistic Assessment of Norepinephrine Therapy versus Angiotensin-II in Septic Shock (MANTRA): Study Protocol for a multicenter randomized trial
